'''Isidore Isaac Hirschman Jr.''' (1922–1990) was an American mathematician, and professor at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] working on [[mathematical analysis|analysis]].

== Life ==
Hirschman earned his Ph.D. in 1947 from Harvard under [[David Widder]]. After writing ten papers together, Hirschman and [[David Widder|Widder]] published a book entitled ''[[The Convolution Transform]]''.<ref name=":0" /> Hirschman spent most of his career (1949–1978) at Washington University, publishing mainly in harmonic analysis and operator theory. Washington University holds a lecture series given by Hirschman, with one lecture given by [[Richard Askey]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url = http://www.maa.org/press/periodicals/convergence/whos-that-mathematician-paul-r-halmos-collection-page-23|title = Who's That Mathematician? Paul R. Halmos Collection – Page 23 {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|website = www.maa.org|access-date = 2016-08-29}}</ref> While Askey was at Washington University, Hirschman asked him to solve an ultraspherical polynomial problem. Askey says in this lecture, "This led to a joint paper, and was what started my interest in special functions."<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url = http://www-groups.dcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/history/Biographies/Askey.html|title = Askey biography|website = www-groups.dcs.st-andrews.ac.uk|access-date = 2016-08-29|archive-date = 2016-09-11|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160911022635/http://www-groups.dcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/history/Biographies/Askey.html|url-status = dead}}</ref>

== Research ==
Hirschman's PhD was entitled “Some Representation and Inversion Problems for the [[Laplace transform|Laplace Transform]],” He mainly published papers in [[harmonic analysis]] and [[operator theory]]. In 1959 Hirschman wrote a paper with Askey,  ''Weighted quadratic norms and ultraspherical polynomials'', published in the ''Transactions of the American Mathematical Society''.<ref name=":1" /> This was one of the two articles Hirschman and Askey co-wrote to complete Hirschman's 1955 research program.<ref name=":1" />

In 1964 Hirschman published ''Extreme eigenvalues of Toeplitz forms associated with Jacobi polynomials'', showing that for <math>n\times n</math> banded [[Toeplitz matrix|Toeplitz matrices]], [[Eigenvalues and eigenvectors|eigenvalues]] accumulate on a spatial curve, in the [[complex plane]] with the normalized eigenvalue counting measure converging weakly to a measure on this curve as <math>n\rightarrow\infty</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hirschman|first=I. I.|date=1964-01-01|title=Extreme eigen values of Toeplitz forms associated with Jacobi polynomials.|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.pjm/1103034367|journal=Pacific Journal of Mathematics|volume=14|issue=1|pages=107–161|doi=10.2140/pjm.1964.14.107 |issn=0030-8730|doi-access=free}}</ref>
